issues.legal_issue: An assessment of a Hindu undivided family is invalid when a partition claim made within a reasonable time is not investigated before the assessment is completed.
material_facts: A member of the family requested that the partition be recorded before the assessments were completed.
The assessments were made against the family without an inquiry into the partition claim.
The Tribunal found that a valid request to record the partition had been made in time.
issues.conclusion: The assessments made without the required inquiry were liable to be set aside on appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Section 25A(1) of the Income Tax Act, 1922 requires an inquiry into a partition claim made by or on behalf of a member of a Hindu undivided family previously assessed as undivided. If no finding is recorded, section 25A(3) deems the family to continue as undivided, but a timely claim cannot be disregarded when making an assessment. The Court distinguished Kalwa Devadattam v. Union of India, which concerned a civil suit rather than an appeal against the assessment; Additional Income-tax Officer, Cuddapah v. A. Thimmayya, which concerned personal liability and tax recovery; and Karri Ramakrishna Reddy v. Tax Recovery Officer, which likewise did not concern an appeal against the assessment itself.

rule.if: assessment_appeal and family_previously_assessed_as_undivided and timely_partition_claim and no_partition_inquiry_before_assessment

predicates.assessment_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal against an assessment made on a Hindu undivided family.
predicates.family_previously_assessed_as_undivided: The family had previously been assessed as undivided.
predicates.timely_partition_claim: A member or representative of the family claimed before assessment that the family property had been partitioned, and the claim was made in time for an inquiry to be undertaken.
predicates.no_partition_inquiry_before_assessment: The assessing authority completed the assessment without investigating the partition claim.

issues.definition: When an assessment appeal concerns a family previously assessed as undivided, and a timely partition claim was not investigated before assessment, the assessment is set aside on appeal.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate authority that sets aside an assessment for failure to investigate a timely partition claim must direct the assessing authority to complete the matter afresh unless the law forbids such a direction.
material_facts: The Tribunal cancelled the assessments for failure to inquire into the partition claim but gave no direction for fresh assessments.
The claim was not established to have been made belatedly.
The statute did not prohibit the appellate authority from directing the assessing authority to dispose of the matter afresh.
issues.conclusion: The Tribunal erred by merely cancelling the assessments; it should have set them aside and directed fresh assessments in accordance with law. The assessments could not instead be upheld with a direction that they be modified.
issues.legal_principle: An appellate authority has both jurisdiction and a duty to correct errors in the proceedings under appeal and, where necessary, to direct the authority below to dispose of the whole or part of the matter afresh, unless the statute forbids it. Because the claim was not shown to be belated and no statutory bar applied, fresh assessments were the proper remedy. The Court did not decide what consequence would follow if a partition claim were made so late that an inquiry could not reasonably be completed before the assessment deadline.

rule.if: assessment_appeal and assessment_set_aside_for_procedural_error and claim_not_shown_belated and law_does_not_forbid_fresh_proceedings_direction

predicates.assessment_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an assessment.
predicates.assessment_set_aside_for_procedural_erro: The appellate authority sets aside the assessment because a required procedure was not followed.
predicates.claim_not_shown_belated: The claim that required consideration was not established to have been made too late for the authority to act on it.
predicates.law_does_not_forbid_fresh_proceedings_di: No applicable legal rule prevents the appellate authority from directing the assessing authority to reconsider the matter.

issues.definition: When an assessment appeal results in setting aside an assessment for procedural error, the claim was not shown to be belated, and fresh proceedings are not forbidden, the appellate authority directs a fresh assessment.
